Equipment:
Forced Draft Fan Motor
Introduction

This document
details the items which are checking. They include testing and the inspections,
in addition to the procedures listed it expected the checks which are done
frequently, would also be completed at
this time.

The first draft
is initiated by eng.Ekramy Mostafa
Mohamad. Accepted by technical expert eng. Hassan Elbehiry and quality
control general director eng. Gamal Abd Elwahab, and approved by eng.
Mohamad Gamal Diab Head sector of Inspection and Quality Control sector.
Safety Precautions

Disconnect all power to
motor prior to initiating any maintenance or repairs.

Avoid contact with rotating
parts.

Act with care in accordance
with prescribed procedures, in handling and lifting this equipment.

Be sure shaft key is fully
captive before unit is energized.

Always be sure oil
lubricated units are filled with correct oil to proper level before operating.

Provide proper safeguards for
personnel against rotating parts and applications involving high inertia loads
which can cause overspeed

sections.text: CHECKS IN CASE OF ABNORMAL OPERATION

In
case of abnormal operation ( for example: heating,
abnormal noise, abnormal current,... ), it is necessary to check the condition
of the different parts of the machine, to dismantle it partially or completely
and to overhaul it.

Particularly,
the cleaning of the inside of the machine, of the rotor and stator ventilation
ducts and of the windings must be carried out with dry, oil free compressed
air, maximum pressure 3 bars.

If
the machine is too dirty, it can be cleaned with a cloth impregnated with turpentine.

After
cleaning, check the insulation resistance of the windings.

Refer
to page "Insulation checks".

sections.text: BEARING LUBRICATION

Oil lubricated bearing
Self-lubricated

Each
bearing is provided with an oil sight glass with the indication of
"mini" and "maxi" oil level.

The
oil level must be between those two marks, motor in idle condition.

Bearing
oil and impurities must be periodically drained before to fill new oil.

For
that purpose the bearing is provided with an oil drain plug.

Oil
must be filtered, or new oil must be put:
6 hours
then 150 hours after the first start-up.
Then the recommended draining interval is : 8000 hours.

Yet it is advised to check periodically
the oil quality, specially after the first start-up.

Oil must be changed as soon as its
color or its viscosity is altered.

AIR FILTER CLEANING
A dirty filter makes the machine to heat.

When the stator temperature over-reaches the
temperature data given in the connection diagram, it is necessary to clean the
filters of the machine.

items: A dirty filter makes the machine to heat.

When the stator temperature over-reaches the
temperature data given in the connection diagram, it is necessary to clean the
filters of the machine.

sections.text: Procedure

The
filters are located in the air inlet.

Unscrew
bolts securing the air inlet panels to the ventilation hood and remove the
panel including the hood.

In order to remove dust out of the filter, clean it with 
compressed air or with water.

If
the filter is too dirty, it can be cleaned with water with addition of sodium
carbonate.

Use
no other detergent.

The
filter must be completely dry before machine start-up.

Dry
the filter with warm air.

SUPPORTS FOR DISMANTLING

When
dismantling a bearing, to remove the parts out of the shaft, use two supports:
A
support "A" placed at the end of the shaft, or eventually at the end
of the extension shaft.
A
support "B" placed as close as possible to the frame.

If
there is not enough space for a support, replace it with a sling.

Make
sure that the supports do not damage the machined parts of the shaft.

sections.text: To take a part out of the shaft:

Bring
the bearing part next to the "A" support.

Put
the "B" support in place, remove the "A" support and then
remove the bearing part.

Put
the "A" support back in place and remove the "B" support.

If
there is enough place, several parts can be removed
simultaneously.

DISMANTLING OF PARTS ASSEMBLED
WITH SEALING PASTE

Some parts like covers, hoods, housings, are put in place
with the jointed sides covered with a coat of sealing paste.

To dismantle these parts, it is necessary to loosen
them after their securing bolts are removed.

For that operation threaded holes are provided:
- in covers, hoods and
housings.
- in end shields to loosen
them.

sections.text: Rotor Dismantling

In
order to remove the rotor, the preliminary operations before dismantling should
be carried out and the bearings must be dismantled.

In
order to handle the rotor, a steel tube should be prepared.

This
tube will be put in the shaft.

The
inside diameters of the tube should be between 3 to 6 mm greater than the shaft
diameters.

Put
a thin copper sheet (between 0.5 and 1 mm) lining its inside, in order to
protect the machined parts.

Length
of tube fitted to the shaft: about 350 mm

Tube
length: about 1500 mm

Place
slings at both ends of rotor + tube and remove the assembly.

Avoid
all stator-rotor contact, which could damage the magnetic circuits and the
windings.

sections.text: Remove the Rotor
Lay the rotor on a mobile trolley,
Remove the slings, take the trolley with the rotor away from the stator, and
Remove the handling tube.

sections.text: Reassembly

Reassemble
the various pieces in reverse order of the steps used for dismantling.

During
reassembly take care that insulated parts do not scrape against iron parts and
that the rotor does not scrape against the stator.

Check
the cleanliness of the various parts.

Put
oil on the surfaces in contact with the shaft and on the sleeve.

Carefully
clean the machined surfaces covered with sealing paste and put some more paste
(Type Hylomar 32M or H for instance) before
reassembly.

Make
sure to put paste on both sides that have to be jointed, place it evenly in
thin coats free of lumps.

Check
that all bolts are well tightened and put the bolt stops.
